subject.title: [Feature]: Support arbitrary workspace files in bootstrap context injection

question: Should OpenClaw support explicitly configured custom-basename workspace files in the bundled bootstrap-extra-files hook?
rationale: The code change is mechanically clear, but it changes which operator-configured files can enter deterministic startup context and therefore needs maintainer intent on the product/security boundary.

options.title: Approve Guarded Custom Files
options.body: Allow custom basenames only when explicitly configured and still protected by workspace containment, size budgets, diagnostics, deterministic ordering, and session filtering.

options.title: Keep Recognized Basenames Only
options.body: Leave the bundled hook restricted to known bootstrap filenames and steer custom context into separate hook/plugin packages or first-class filename proposals.

options.title: Defer To Broader Context Design
options.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers choose a larger context-files, session-filtering, or capability-discovery API.

recommendation.title: Approve Guarded Custom Files
recommendation.body: Allow custom basenames only when explicitly configured and still protected by workspace containment, size budgets, diagnostics, deterministic ordering, and session filtering.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete merged the original hook feature and has adjacent boundary-read history, making him the best available owner for the contract decision.
